Our NFL Player Prop Bet Cheat Sheet assists bettors by comparing lines from leading sportsbooks with our daily NFL projections. What is an NFL player prop bet? An NFL player prop bet is a type of wager where you’re betting on the performance of a specific player in a game rather than the overall outcome. For example, you might place a bet on how many passing yards a quarterback will throw for, or how many touchdowns a running back will score. It’s a fun way to get more invested in the action, especially if you’re confident in how a particular player will perform, regardless of who wins or loses the game. results.title: 2026 NFL Week 11 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Bucs Are Live As Touchdown Underdogs
results.description: Geoff Schwartz likes Tampa Bay to keep it close in Detroit and has a Christian McCaffrey prop for Vikings-49ers in Mexico City.
highlights: 2026 NFL Week 11 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Bucs Are Live As Touchdown Underdogs Kirk Cousins was the story of Week 10. Now the Vikings get their biggest test yet. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports. The Vikings are a different team with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. We saw last weekend that average quarterback play can turn a struggling, inept offense into a group that scores like an average NFL offense. It feels easy to take Minnesota again against San Francisco in Mexico City. However, I'm going to skip the side and total in favor of a prop. The 49ers rely on Christian McCaffrey as the workhorse of their offense, and that was on full display last weekend. He had 13 carries for just over 60 yards and added four catches for 161 yards. I'm targeting his receptions number in this game.

The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. One way to combat that pressure is to get the running back out of the backfield quickly and find him on mismatches. We saw it last week when McCaffrey got matched up on Von Miller for a touchdown. I think the 49ers have to use McCaffrey in the passing game to have success against Minnesota's pressure. I like the Over on his receptions. This line could reflect Tampa Bay possibly being without quarterback Baker Mayfield, who is questionable with multiple injuries. However, I believe Mayfield will play, with the Bucs still in the hunt for a division title. He's a tough guy, and he won't miss this game. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Detroit's defense is without its two best players: Jack Campbell is unavailable, and star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured last week.

The Lions' pass rush is significantly worse without Hutchinson, and any team, including the Bucs, will take advantage of it. No Lions lead will be safe moving forward. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover.

results.description: Eagles upsetting the Steelers? Big receiving day for Christian McCaffrey? Touchdown for Josh Downs? Let's predict 15 things for Week 11.
highlights: So when Minnesota brings the heat in Mexico City, Purdy is going to be looking for his star running back ... a lot. Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals: 31-of-39, 378 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 sacks, 91 QBR I know this is chalky considering the heater Burrow is on, but I feel especially confident that he will put up numbers against the Commanders. Washington blitzes 42% of the time, the third-highest rate in the league, but somehow has a below average pass rush win rate. That is quite the indictment on its ability to disrupt the opposing quarterback. And it's an especially bad combination against Burrow, who is thriving even more when blitzed (86 QBR) than when not (77 QBR) in 2026. Burrow has also become quite adept at sack avoidance (4.4% sack rate), which is partially a reflection of better pass protection this season.

Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Texans defeated the Colts on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 12 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts. First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs that could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Eagles pull off an upset over the Steelers? Is 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey in for a big receiving day against the Vikings? Does Titans quarterback Cam Ward have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? Will we see another touchdown for wide receiver Josh Downs in a Chiefs uniform? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action. Maldonado predicts two upsets Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday. Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard Mason McCormick (ankle). Eagles backup QB Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver DeVonta Smith potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.
